html:
SMTO-CTR-0017 — Your request changed while SMTO was writing its plan

GUID: 9334a7c7-9ef8-416b-885d-66d1f4052df4
Slug: task-contract-stale-source-revision
Domain: CTR · Subsystem: task-contract

What happened

  • You added to or changed your request while SMTO was still writing its plan, so SMTO threw that plan away instead of using an out-of-date one. Nothing was done with the old plan.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Watch the task for a few seconds. It should show Generating task contract again, this time using your latest message. SMTO drops the out-of-date plan and plans again from the updated request.
  2. If the task looks stuck, reload the page in your browser to see its current state. The page may still be showing the plan that was thrown away.
  3. If the task has stopped and no new plan appears, send your complete, final request again as a new message. A fresh message makes SMTO plan from the version you actually want, not an older one.

What success looks like

  • The task shows Task contract generated and starts working on your latest request.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't select Retry in an older tab or window; it belongs to the plan that was thrown away and SMTO will refuse it.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Task Contract acceptance found the source changed during generation (a newer amendment, a superseded decision generation or a different source identity), so the attempt was marked stale and its contract was not installed.

What this means

  • Acceptance observes changed source identity, a newer amendment, or an attempt already marked stale before installing its contract. This failure does not authorize execution for the rejected contract revision. Earlier revisions may already have effects; their original receipts remain authoritative. Diagnostic rendering makes no compiler or integrity-model call.

Why this can happen

  • Acceptance observes changed source identity, a newer amendment, or an attempt already marked stale before installing its contract.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare attempt/source revision with the latest accepted user amendment and Stop state.

How to fix it

  • NativeCompilationSession.acceptance (src/agent_runtime/native/task_contract_session.py) yielded False, or _run_compiler_attempt saw a different source identity, so the attempt was saved with validation_state 'stale' and reason stale_source_revision. The run loop normally recompiles from the latest amendment via prepare_turn; if the run ended instead, reload the run snapshot, compare the attempt's source_digest with the current amendment_seq and Stop state, and submit from the current source rather than reusing the stale attempt ID.
  • Refresh the current source and use its supported compilation controls.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • Only a contract compiled from the intended current source is installed.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • This failure does not authorize execution for the rejected contract revision. Earlier revisions may already have effects; their original receipts remain authoritative. Diagnostic rendering makes no compiler or integrity-model call.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
